newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks soar to end morning in record territory.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks soar to end morning in record territory.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks soared to finish the Thursday morning session in record territory, thrust higher by bullish overseas market trends and positive outlooks for the economy's main sectors, analysts and brokers said.

"Property is driving the index at the moment," said Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel. "In addition, what you have is a (U.S.) bond yield of 6.33 percent and figures coming out of the U.S. indicating there will be no rise in interest rates."
The Hang Seng Index ended the morning up 326.29 points, or 2.04 percent, at 16,309.47, just off the all-time high of 16,310.17 hit before the end of the early session.

The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond closed trading in New York on Wednesday 26/32 higher at 103-30/32 to yield 6.33 percent, and some U.S. economists have revised their expectations for the issue's yield downside to 5.5 percent, brokers said.
The trend suggests a prolonged period of low interest rates for the United States and Hong Kong, brokers said.
The Dow Industrials set a new closing high of 8,254.89.

"The property news is pretty good," said McAllister, refering to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's announcement earlier in the week that it saw no need to restrict banks' property-related lending at this time.

The property sector led the market's record-breaking advance. The commercial and industrial sector, which has a heavy reliance on property earnings, followed. China-incorporated H-shares were also strong.
Property developer Cheung Kong was the most active share, leaping HK$4.50 to HK$85.25 on heavy trade of HK$1.13 billion.
"Cheung Kong is up because of Hutchison," said Adrian Ngan, director at Peregrine Securities. "One week ago Hutchison was trading at HK$65.00, now it is HK$75.00."
Conglomerate Hutchison Whampoa added HK$2.00 to HK$75.75.

"Since Cheung Kong holds 1.8 billion shares or roughly 50 percent of Hutchison, Cheung Kong's NAV (net asset value) has risen by HK$18 billion, or HK$8.00 to HK$9.00 per share in just the past week," said Ngan.
HSBC Holdings jumped HK$5.00 to HK$268.00, spurred by continuing optimism about the banking sector's prospects.
H-share Shanghai Petrochemicals advanced HK$0.20 to HK$2.50 after the suspension of trade in shares of Yizheng Chemical.
Brokers said the market was awash with rumours about restructuring of the Yizheng group and mergers among other players in China's petrochemical industry to strengthen competitiveness.
